subject: Request: temporary p95 grace + measurement-horizon clarification
messages:
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@nimblepay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: sudden burst — request for temporary p95 grace + measurement horizon details

Hi Naomi,

Quick context: we cut over a subset of payment flows to a new routing provider yesterday and saw multiple short-duration bursts to Redwood hosted inference that pushed our observed p95 above the contracted target. The spikes were short (many samples under 30s) but enough to trip our alert and trigger an SLA notice in our own monitoring.

We need two things from Redwood ASAP:
1) Confirmation of the hosted API measurement horizon and aggregation rules you will use for any p50/p95 determination (sliding window? fixed epoch?), and whether transient short bursts are eligible for carveouts;
2) A request for a temporary p95 grace (7 days) while we finish mitigations on our side — this is customer-impacting but short-lived. We will provide raw request traces and sampling slices.

I attached a CSV with raw latency samples for the last 36 hours (nimblepay_burst_metrics_nov09.csv) and a signed request form with our expected mitigation timeline.

Can you let us know the evidence you need from us and what Redwood can do to reduce the risk (routing tweaks, cache warm, canary isolation)? We appreciate a quick acknowledgement; our ops team is standing by.

Thanks,
Alex Garner
Head of Platform Reliability, NimblePay
alex.garner@nimblepay.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachment: nimblepay_temp_relief_request_form.pdf (PDF, 92 KB)

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: sudden burst — request for temporary p95 grace + measurement horizon details

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and the data. We can move fast on this. Short answers up front:

- Measurement baseline: Hosted p50/p95 on contracts is calculated from 5-minute buckets aggregated into a rolling 24-hour window for reporting, with percentile calculation over the sampling set in that window. We also maintain per-customer request volume weighting so large bursts can skew the p95 if they represent significant token counts.
- Carveouts: transient short bursts are considered for transient carveouts on a case-by-case basis; we require sampling evidence and operational context (traffic source, start/end times, and mitigation steps).

Proposed immediate plan:
1) We can approve a provisional 7-day p95 grace beginning once we confirm the sample set and can reproduce the burst in our logs. This will be treated as a controlled exception tied to the ticket INC-7921 (see Jira link).
2) To minimize user impact while the exception is in effect, we will:
   - Route NimblePay requests preferentially to a warmed pool with reduced batching to lower tail latency for the next 72 hours;
   - Enable per-customer prefix caching for common prompts where applicable;
   - Stand up a small canary route (10% traffic) to validate mitigations before promoting to 100%.
3) We need 24 hours of request traces from your side broken into the following slices: pre-burst, burst window (start/end), and a post-burst slice. If you can provide request IDs and approximate token counts that will accelerate alignment.

I'll initiate the provisional exception after a quick verification step from our SRE (Karthik) and PM (Marissa). Karthik — can you confirm log-retention access and the fastest way to match their request IDs to our tracing? Marissa — I'll need a one-paragraph summary for the exception ticket to include with the audit trail.

I'll attach a short mitigation checklist we plan to execute.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Subject: Re: sudden burst — request for temporary p95 grace + measurement horizon details

Naomi / Marissa — quick technical note from SRE: we have log retention and tracing that can map NimblePay request IDs to our backend request IDs within ~2 hours if NimblePay includes the client_request_id header (or 24 hours if we need to do heuristic matching by timestamp+ip). For quick triage I'll spin up a query to pull the affected 5-minute buckets for the times in the CSV.

Countermeasures we can apply immediately (if Naomi greenlights):
- Warm an isolated pool on the current model variant for NimblePay (adds some cost but reduces tail latency).
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size for that pool to bias towards lower tail but slightly higher per-token cost.
- Bind a small, high-priority route that avoids cross-tenant batching for 48–72 hours.

If Alex can surface the earliest burst window (to the minute) and include any client_request_id values, we'll match traces and expedite the provisional exception.

-Karthik
